storylines.title: Prologue: The Leaf and the Fire
storylines.about: Virginia, 2767, told by the King in Rome. The Free Assembly rises against Church and Crown, and begins with fire.

still.caption: The King's study in Rome, by candlelight: the war map on the desk, the dome of Saint Peter's in the window.

lines: Sit by me. The map on the table is the world as it was when I was young.
Everything I am going to tell you began on one plantation in Virginia.
Fairleigh ended it in a single morning, and we called it over.
Look at the map again. The fire did not stay in Virginia.
I was a seminarian then, waiting for my ship to Rome. I read Augustine under an oak.
The men in the fields talked of an Assembly. I did not understand what they wanted.
I still smell the smoke when I close my eyes.
Two letters came for the Governor that week: one from an explorer in the Amazon, one from a clockmaker. He gave them to me to read.
The harvest is in the barns. A fortune hangs in those rafters, and every rebel in the county knows it.
Study the war table. Then we wait for the night.
It is done. I take no pleasure in it.
Ruggieri has his pipe, and I have the King's leaf. Rome will hear of this.

storylines.title: The Explorer
storylines.about: A Catholic explorer goes down into the deep earth and finds the Brood. (Being written.)

still.caption: Dr. Lindqvist's research station on the Amazon: the specimen chart of the plateau on the table, the jars glowing green, rain on the forest outside.

lines: Do not tap the glass. It sleeps, and I would like it to go on sleeping.
The Academy wants specimens. I want to understand them. The plateau will give us both.
An egg from the plateau under a bell jar, warm to the touch.
Lindqvist writes down its weight every morning. It grows.
A young creature in spirits, coiled like a question. The label says only: Plateau, specimen four.

storylines.title: The Clockmaker
storylines.about: A clockmaker grows afraid of his own Clockwork. (Being written.)

still.caption: Meister Hollweg's workshop in Nuremberg by lantern light: the brass map of the world on its table, the great clock of the Guild.

lines: Mind your sleeve near the table. The map turns, and every ring of it is a road, a river or a sea.
The Crown pays the Guild for patience. My machines have more of it than any soldier.
The great clock of the Guild of the Escapement. It has not lost a second in forty years.
Hollweg says a city could be kept the same way.
A labouring automaton, half finished. Its hands are a smith's; its face is left blank.
